claims.text: The initial catalyst is a nanoscale equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
All six constituent elements are uniformly distributed at the catalyst surface.
The intervention reduces surface Rh concentration by 30–40% relative to the equimolar baseline while preserving the relative ratios of Pt, Pd, Ru, Ir, and Os.
Moderate Rh depletion disrupts critical Rh-containing surface atomic ensembles.
Rh-containing ensembles provide optimal adsorption energies for oxygenated ethanol-oxidation intermediates such as CH3CO* and CH3CHO*.
Rh-containing ensembles stabilize reaction intermediates and thereby direct ethanol oxidation along a particular pathway.
Disruption of Rh-containing ensembles alters intermediate adsorption energies.
Altered adsorption energies modify the rate-determining steps of ethanol oxidation.
Rh depletion is associated with changes in lattice strain and shifts in the d-band center.
The Rh-depleted catalyst will exhibit a changed product distribution, likely including increased acetaldehyde yield.
The Rh-depleted catalyst will exhibit shifts in ethanol-oxidation onset potential and changes in current density.
Disruption of Rh sites may improve durability by reducing catalyst poisoning.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at 30–40% relative Rh depletion, 0.5–0.8 V versus RHE, in acidic electrolyte at ambient temperature.
Keeping catalyst loading, electrode preparation, synthesis, and reaction conditions identical permits comparison with the equimolar baseline.
In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy can track the proposed changes in local coordination and electronic structure, including d-band-center shifts.
Pairing the intervention with in situ characterization ensures that performance changes can be causally attributed to Rh content and its local environment.
Subtle global restructuring caused by Rh depletion cannot be completely ruled out.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that the paired intervention and characterization ensure causal attribution to Rh content and its local environment, whereas the uncertainty field concedes that broader structural or electronic changes cannot be isolated completely.

The falsification rule treats failure to achieve selective Rh-ensemble disruption, or observation of widespread restructuring, as falsification. Such a result instead represents failure of the intended intervention or violation of the mechanism's stated premise, not a decisive test of the proposed causal mechanism.
